newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinians on hunger strike on Egypt border.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians on hunger strike on Egypt border.

text.p: Palestinian refugees stranded for more than a year at a desert camp on the Egypt-Libya border have started a hunger strike to protest against their plight, Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) said on Wednesday.
"Young men, among whom are students, started a hunger strike four days ago as a demonstration of despair," it said in a statement.
A security source at the border said some people put a sign outside their tent saying they were on hunger strike.

Hundreds of Palestinians have been stranded at the camp since September 1995, when Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi expelled thousands of Palestinians in a bid to show the futility of their leaders' peace accords with Israel.
Many Palestinians have since returned to the Palestinian self-rule areas but those without the papers needed to enter either Egypt or the Gaza Strip and West Bank remain stranded.
Egypt has refused to allow in any of the Palestinians at the camp unless they have travel documents to other countries. It has made some exceptions in case of medical emergencies.

MSF, which has two workers in the camp, said the refugees face a second winter of freezing temperatures in flimsy tents. The medical charity also said security forces controlling the checkpoints regularly harass the inhabitants.

Tight security was imposed on the camp earlier this week when Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak travelled by land to Libya for talks with Gaddafi. The security measures were enacted to prevent the refugees from staging a protest.
The makeshift camp is on the road that connects the two countries.
